sections.english: This is wickedness: this is what you have often seen. And you should have this thought ready to hand against any eventuality: 'I have seen this often before.' Generally wherever you look you will find the same things. The histories — ancient, more recent, modern — are full of them: whole cities and households are full of them today. There is nothing new: all is familiar and quickly over.
sections.chinese: 此即邪恶：此乃你所常见之事。你当常备此念以应万变：「此事我以前已屡见不鲜。」概而言之，无论你往何处看，所见者皆同。史乘之中——远者、近者、今者——充斥此类事：今日之全城全家亦充塞此类事。世间原无新事：一切皆已成惯见，且转眼即逝。

sections.english: Your principles are living things. How else could they be deadened, except by the extinction of the corresponding mental images? And the constant rekindling of these is up to you. 'I am able to form the judgement I should about this event. If able, why should I be troubled? Things outside my understanding have no relation to my understanding.' Learn this, and you are upright. Recovery of life is possible. Look at things again as you used to look at them. Recovery of life consists in this.
sections.chinese: 你之原则乃是活物。它们怎能被杀死，除了那相应之心象被扑灭？而不断重新点燃这些心象，全在你。于此事件我能形成所当形之判断。若能为，我何须烦恼？我之理解外之事物，与我之理解毫无关涉。学此一事，便是挺直了。恢复生命是可能的。再来一次，以你从前看待事物之眼光看待它们。恢复生命即在于此。

sections.english: The empty pomp of a procession, plays on the stage, flocks and herds, jousting shows, a bone thrown to puppies, tit-bits into the fishponds, ants toiling and carrying, the scurries of frightened mice, puppets dancing on their strings. Well, amid all this you must keep your good humour and not be patronizing. But realize that a man's worth is no greater than the worth of his ambitions.
sections.chinese: 游行队列之空洞盛况、舞台之戏目、畜群牲队、枪矛竞技之观演、掷给幼犬之骨、投进鱼池之精料、蚁群劳碌与搬运、惊鼠之窜逃、傀儡牵线之舞。身处此诸般之中，你当保你之好兴致而不居高临下。然亦须明白：一人之价值，不逾其抱负之价值。

sections.english: In conversation one ought to follow closely what is said, in any impulse to follow closely what takes place. In the latter case, to see immediately the intended object of reference: in the former, to watch carefully what is meant.
sections.chinese: 谈话之时，当紧随所言之内容；任何冲动中，当紧随所发生之事。在后者中，当即看到所指向之目标；在前者中，当细察所意谓者为何。

sections.english: Is my mind sufficient for this task, or is it not? If it is, I use it for the task as an instrument given me by the nature of the Whole. If it is not, I either cede the work (if it is otherwise my responsibility) to someone better able to accomplish it, or, if that is not proper, I do it as best I can, calling on the help of one who can use my directing mind to effect what is timely and beneficial for the community.
sections.chinese: 我心智足应付此事否？若足，则我将其用作宇宙整体之本性所赐我之工具来完成此任务。若不足，我则将此工作（若其在其他意义上乃我之职责）让与更能胜任之人，或若此举不妥，便尽我之所能为之，同时吁请那人来援助——他能运用我的主导之心智，为共同体成就那适时而有益之事。

sections.english: How many who once rose to fame are now consigned to oblivion: and how many who sang their fame are long disappeared.
sections.chinese: 多少曾煊赫一时之人，如今已交付遗忘：多少曾咏唱其名者，亦早已杳然无踪。

sections.english: Do not be ashamed of help. It is your task to achieve your assigned duty, like a soldier in a scaling-party. What, then, if you are lame and cannot climb the parapet by yourself, but this is made possible by another's help?
sections.chinese: 勿以接受帮助为羞。你之任务乃完成指派于你之职责，犹如一攻城之士兵。那么，若你瘸腿而不能独自攀登墙垣，而藉他人之助却可达成，又有何妨？

sections.english: Do not let the future trouble you. You will come to it (if that is what you must) possessed of the same reason that you apply now to the present.
sections.chinese: 毋让未来困扰于你。你走向它时（若那是你必行之途），将带着与你此时运用于当下之相同的理性。

sections.english: All things are meshed together, and a sacred bond unites them. Hardly a single thing is alien to the rest: ordered together in their places they together make up the one order of the universe. There is one universe out of all things, one god pervading all things, one substance, one law, one reason common to all intelligent creatures, and one truth.
sections.chinese: 万物彼此紧扣相织，一神圣之纽带联结着它们。几乎没有一物与他者相异陌：各居其位，有序汇聚，它们一同构成宇宙之单一秩序。由万物而成一宇宙，一神普彻透贯万物，一实体，一法律，一切智性生灵所共有之一理性，以及一真理。

sections.english: Everything material rapidly disappears in the universal substance; every cause is rapidly taken up into the universal reason; and the memory of everything is rapidly buried in eternity.
sections.chinese: 一切物质者皆迅速地消逝于宇宙实体之中；一切原因皆迅速地被摄入那宇宙理性之中；一切事物之记忆皆迅速地被埋没于永恒之中。

sections.english: For a rational being, to act in accordance with nature is also to act in accordance with reason.
sections.chinese: 于理性存在者而言，依照自然而行动，即是依照理性而行动。

sections.english: Standing straight — or held straight.
sections.chinese: 自行直立——或被扶直。

sections.english: Rational beings collectively have the same relation as the various limbs of an organic unity — they were created for a single cooperative purpose. The notion of this will strike you more forcefully if you keep on saying to yourself: 'I am a limb of the composite body of rational beings.'
sections.chinese: 众理性存在者集合在一起，其彼此间之关系，犹如一有机整体之诸般肢体——彼等乃为一个单一的协作目的而被造。如果你不断对己说「我是那由理性存在者所组成之复合躯体的一肢体」，则此观念将更加有力地冲击于你。

sections.english: Let any external thing that so wishes happen to those parts of me which can be affected by its happening — and they, if they wish, can complain. I myself am not yet harmed, unless I judge this occurrence something bad: and I can refuse to do so.
sections.chinese: 凡外在事物所愿加之事，便加诸我身上那些能被其发生所影响之部分吧——彼等部分，若情愿，自可抱怨。我自己并未受伤害，除非我将此事判断为坏事：而我能够拒不作此判断。

sections.english: Whatever anyone does or says, I must be a good man. It is as if an emerald, or gold or purple, were always saying: 'Whatever anyone does or says, I must be an emerald and keep my own colour.'
sections.chinese: 无论何人做何事、言何语，我必须是一个好人。就如同一块绿宝石、或黄金、或紫袍，恒常说：「无论何人做何事、言何语，我必须是一块绿宝石，保持我自身之色泽。」

sections.english: The directing mind does not disturb itself: for example, it does not frighten itself or lead itself to desire. If anyone else can frighten it or cause it pain, let him do so: of itself, of its own judgement, it will not deliberately turn to such modes.
sections.chinese: 主导之心智不会自我搅扰：譬如其不自吓，亦不引己入欲望之途。若任何别人能吓它或使之痛苦，那人便去做吧：就其自身、凭其自己之判断，它不会蓄意转向此种情境。

sections.english: Happiness is a benign god or divine blessing. Why then, my imagination, are you doing what you do? Go away, in the gods' name, the way you came: I have no need of you. You have come in your old habit. I am not angry with you. Only go away.
sections.chinese: 幸福乃是仁慈之神明或神灵之赐福。那么，我的幻念，你为何做你所做之事？以诸神之名，从你来的路上离去吧：我不需要你。你按你之旧习惯而来。我不对你生气。只是离去吧。

sections.english: Is someone afraid of change? Well, what can ever come to be without change? Or what is dearer or closer to the nature of the Whole than change? Can you yourself take your bath, if the wood that heats it is not changed? Can you be fed, unless what you eat is changed? Can any other useful thing be achieved without change? Do you not see then that for yourself a change similar to theirs is both necessary and necessary to the nature of the Whole?
sections.chinese: 难道有人害怕变化？然而，若无变化，何物能生成？又有什么比变化更亲于、更近于宇宙整体之本性？你自己能沐浴，若加热水之木柴未经变化？你能进食，除非你吃掉之物被消化变化？任何其他有用之物，若无变化，能得以成就？你难道看不见，于你自己，与万物类似之变化，既是必须的，亦为宇宙整体本性所必须？

sections.english: All our bodies pass through the universal substance as through a swirling stream. How many a Chrysippus, a Socrates, an Epictetus has eternity already swallowed! The same thought will apply to every man and thing.
sections.chinese: 吾辈一切躯体，皆穿过宇宙实体如穿过一涡旋之流。多少克律西波斯、苏格拉底、爱比克泰德，永恒早已吞没！此一念，适用于每一人和每一物。

sections.english: I have only one anxiety: that I myself should not do something which the human constitution does not intend — or does not intend in this way or at this time.
sections.chinese: 我只有唯一之忧：我自己不要做任何不属于人类构造所意愿之事——或非以人类构造之意愿方式、在此时间所做之事。

sections.english: Soon you will have forgotten all things: soon all things will have forgotten you.
sections.chinese: 须臾之间，你便将遗忘一切：须臾之间，一切便将遗忘你。

sections.english: It is human nature to love even those who trip and fall. This follows if you reflect at the time that all men are brothers; that they go wrong through ignorance, not intent; that in a short while both you and they will be dead; and, above all, that the man has done you no harm — he has not made your directing mind worse than it was before.
sections.chinese: 怜爱那些跌倒犯错之人，亦是人类之本性。若你彼时思及：众人皆为兄弟；他们因无知而非蓄意才犯错；不消多时，你与他们皆将死去；而尤重要者，那人并未伤害到你——他并未使你的主导心灵变得比以前更坏。若这般思想，你便会如此。

sections.english: Universal nature uses the substance of the universe like wax, making now the model of a horse, then melting it down and using its material for a tree; next for a man; next for something else. Each one of these subsists for only the briefest time. It is no more a hardship for the chest to be broken up than it was to be put together.
sections.chinese: 宇宙之本性运用宇宙之实体如同蜡脂，当下塑成一匹马之模型，随即融而化之，用其材料再造成一株树；接着塑造一人；接着又塑造他物。其中每一者之存续皆仅最短之时段。箱匣之被拆散，不比它被拼合时更为艰难。

sections.english: A deep scowl on the face is contrary to nature, and when it becomes habitual expressiveness begins to die or is even finally extinguished beyond rekindling. Try to attend to this very point, that this is something against reason. In the field of moral offence, if the very consciousness of doing wrong is gone, what reason is left for living?
sections.chinese: 面上深蹙之眉乃违背自然，当其成为习惯，面部之表意能力便开始枯死，甚至最终熄灭至于无可复燃。你当努力关注此一关键点——此乃违背理性之事。在道德过失之领域，若连犯错之意识都已丧失，那活着还有什么理由？

sections.english: All that you see will in a moment be changed by the nature which governs the Whole: it will create other things out of this material, and then again others out of that, so that the world is always young.
sections.chinese: 你所见之一切，顷刻间便将由统御宇宙整体之本性所改变：它将由此一材料创造出另外之物，然后又由那物再造出另外之物，如此，则世界永葆青春。

sections.english: When someone does you some wrong, you should consider immediately what judgement of good or evil led him to wrong you. When you see this, you will pity him, and not feel surprise or anger. You yourself either still share his view of good, or something like it: you should then forgive him. But if you now judge differently, it will be easy for you to be gracious to one so mistaken.
sections.chinese: 当有人对你行了不义之事，你当立即思量：是什么样之善恶判断导致了他来伤害你。一旦认清此事，你便将怜悯他，而不是感到意外或愤怒。你自己要么仍与他持相同的善之观念，或类似之观念：那你便该原谅他。但若你如今已作不同之判断，你便不难对如此出错之人施以宽仁。

sections.english: Do not dream of possession of what you do not have: rather reflect on the greatest blessings in what you do have, and on their account remind yourself how much they would have been missed if they were not there. But at the same time you must be careful not to let this sense of contentment lead you into overvaluing them, so that you would be distressed if you ever lost them.
sections.chinese: 勿梦寐以求你所不拥有之物：而当思量你现有之物中至大之福祉，并因此念及它们倘若不在、你将会何等若有所失。但与此同时，你亦当小心，勿令此一满足之感引你至过分珍视它们之地步，以致一旦失去它们你便悲苦不宁。

sections.english: Withdraw into yourself. It is in the nature of the rational directing mind to be self-content with acting rightly and the calm it thereby enjoys.
sections.chinese: 退归于己。理性之主导心灵其本性即是：于端正行事及其所随之享有之安宁中，自我安足。

sections.english: Erase the print of imagination. Stop the puppet-strings of impulse. Define the present moment of time. Recognize what happens to you or to another. Analyse and divide the event into the causal and the material. Think of your final hour. Leave the wrong done by that man where the wrong arose.
sections.chinese: 抹去想象之印痕。止住冲动之提线木偶。界定时间之当下此刻。辨识发生在你或他人身上的事。将该事件分析并划分为原因与物质二者。思及你的最后一刻。将那人所行之错，留在那错生起的地方。

sections.english: Stretch your thought to parallel what is being said. Let your mind get inside what is happening and who is doing it.
sections.chinese: 延伸你之思想，与所言之语平行并进。令你的心灵进入正在发生之事，以及那正在行事之人之中。

sections.english: Take your joy in simplicity, in integrity, in indifference to all that lies between virtue and vice. Love mankind. Follow god. Democritus says, 'All else is subject to the law of convention: only the elements are absolute and real' — but enough for you to remember that all things are as nothing.
sections.chinese: 在素朴中取悦，在正直中取悦，在对德行与恶行之间一切事物之不执不染中取悦。爱人类。追随神明。德谟克利特说：「其他一切皆服从于人为约定之律法：唯元素是真实而绝对者」——然于你而言，记住一切皆若虚无，便已足够。

sections.english: On death. Either dispersal, if we are atoms: or, if we are a unity, extinction or a change of home.
sections.chinese: 论死亡。或为离散，若我们仅是原子；或若我辈是一统一体，则为灭绝或迁居。

sections.english: On pain. Unbearable pain carries us off: chronic pain can be borne. The mind preserves its own serenity by withdrawal, and the directing reason is not impaired by pain. It is for the parts injured by the pain to protest if they can.
sections.chinese: 论痛苦。不堪忍受之苦会夺走我们的生命；慢性之痛则可以承受。心灵藉由退转而保持其自在之宁静，主导理性并不为痛苦所损。因痛苦而受伤之部分，若其能够，自可抗议。

sections.english: On fame. Look at their minds, the nature of their thought and what they seek or avoid. And see how, just as drifting sands constantly overlay the previous sand, so in our lives what we once did is very quickly covered over by subsequent layers.
sections.chinese: 论名声。审视那些人之心，其思之性质，以及其所寻索或回避者。且看，正如流沙不断覆没先前之沙，吾辈生命中昔日所为亦很快被其后之层累所掩覆。

sections.english: So, to a man endowed with noble intelligence and a vision of all time and all being, do you think that this human life will seem of great importance? 'Impossible,' he said. So such a man will not think there is anything fearful in death either? 'Certainly not.'
sections.chinese: 那么，于一个拥有高贵智识、堪能观照一切时间与一切存有者之人，你以为此一人之生命会是桩大不了的事吗？「绝不可能，」他答。那么这样一个人也不会认为死有什么可畏了？「当然不会。」

sections.english: A king's lot: to do good and be damned.
sections.chinese: 为君者之命运：行善于世，而横遭毁谤。

sections.english: It is shameful that the face should be so obedient, shaping and ordering its expression as the mind dictates, when the mind cannot impose its own shape and order on itself.
sections.chinese: 面容如此顺从——依心灵之指示而塑造并规整其表情——而心灵竟不能将自身之形态与秩序施加于己，这真是可耻。

sections.english: 'Ripe ears of corn are reaped, and so are lives: One stands, another falls.'
sections.chinese: 「成熟之谷穗被收割，生命亦复如此：一株挺立，另一株倒下。」

sections.english: 'If I and my two sons are now no more The gods' concern, this too will have its cause.'
sections.chinese: 「若我与我的两个儿子如今已不再为诸神所眷顾，此事亦必有其因由。」

sections.english: 'For good and right stand on my side.'
sections.chinese: 「因善与正道立于我之一侧。」

sections.english: But I could give this man a proper answer. I would say: 'You are mistaken, my friend, if you think that a man of any worth at all should take into account the risk of life or death, and not have as his sole consideration in any action whether he is acting justly or unjustly, the part of a good man or a bad man.'
sections.chinese: 但我能给这人一恰当之答复。我会说：「我的朋友，你错了，若你认为一个有半丝价值之人当计及生命与死亡之风险，而不是在每一行动中唯独关心他是义还是不义地行动，是善人之行还是恶人之行。」

sections.english: The truth of the matter, my fellow Athenians, is this. Whatever position a man has taken up in his own best judgement, or is assigned by his commander, there, it seems to me, he should stay and face the danger, giving no thought to death or anything else before dishonour.
sections.chinese: 事实之真相，吾雅典同胞，乃在于是。一个人无论以其自身最佳判断而选定之位置，抑或为其指挥官所分派之哨位，在我看来，他就应当守在那里并面对危险，丝毫不计及死亡或任何其他事——除了耻辱之外。

sections.english: But, my dear fellow, consider it possible that nobility and virtue are something other than saving one's life or having it saved. Could it not be that anyone who is truly a man should dismiss any concern for a particular length of life, and not simply cling to life?
sections.chinese: 然而，我亲爱的朋友，不妨考虑：高贵与德性或许不是保住性命或任人拯救之事。难道，一个真正之人才应当释去对特定寿数长短之任何执念，并且不单纯地贪执生命，不是这样的吗？

sections.english: Observe the movement of the stars as if you were running their courses with them, and let your mind constantly dwell on the changes of the elements into each other. Such imaginings wash away the filth of life on the ground.
sections.chinese: 观想星辰之运行，仿佛你与之同行其轨道一般，并使你之心智时时驻于诸元素彼此互变之中。如此之想象可洗尽地上生命之尘垢。

sections.english: Further, when your talk is about mankind, view earthly things as if looking down on them from some point high above — flocks, armies, farms, weddings, divorces, births, deaths, the hubbub of the law-courts, desert places, various foreign nations, festivals, funerals, markets: all the medley of the world and the harmonious order of opposites.
sections.chinese: 此外，当你谈及人类时，不妨观世间万物如自高处某一地点俯瞰而下——羊群、军队、田庄、婚娶、离异、诞生、死亡、讼庭之喧哗、荒漠之所、诸般异族、节庆、葬仪、集市：世间一切混杂之万象，以及对立者彼此和谐之秩序。

sections.english: Look back over the past — all those many changes of dynasties. And you can foresee the future too: it will be completely alike, incapable of deviating from the rhythm of the present. So for the study of human life forty years are as good as ten thousand years: what more will you see?
sections.chinese: 回望过去——那一切朝代更迭之层出不穷。你也能预见未来：它将完全一致，无法偏离当前之韵律。故于人类生命之研习，四十年或一万年并无分别：你还能看见更多什么吗？

sections.english: Better at throwing his man: but not more public-spirited, or more decent, or more disciplined to circumstance, or more tolerant of neighbours' faults.
sections.chinese: 更善于摔倒对手：却并未更热心公益，亦未更端正，亦未更善于随境自约，亦未对邻人之过更加容耐。

sections.english: Where a task can be accomplished in accordance with the reason which gods and men share, there is nothing to be afraid of: because where there is the possibility of benefit from an action which moves along the proper path, following our own human constitution, there is no place for fear of any harm.
sections.chinese: 若一件事可依照神人所共有的理性来完成，那便无所可畏：因为凡有可能从一沿着正途、遵循吾辈人类自身构造之行动中获益之处，便毫无恐惧任何伤害之余地。

sections.english: Everywhere and all the time it is up to you to honour god in contentment with your present circumstance, to treat the men who are your present company with justice, and to lavish thought on every present impression in your mind, so that nothing slips into your mind without proper analysis.
sections.chinese: 随时随地，你都可以于满足现前之境中虔敬神明，以正义对待你当下所伴之人，并以细致之思倾注于你心中每一当下之印象，令无一物未经恰当之分析便滑入你的心中。

sections.english: Do not look around at the directing minds of other people, but keep looking straight ahead to where nature is leading you — both universal nature, in what happens to you, and your own nature, in what you must do yourself. Every creature must do what follows from its own constitution.
sections.chinese: 莫左右环视他人之主导心灵，而径直注视自然正引领你前往之处——既看那宇宙之自然，于临到你身之事中；也看那你自己之自然，在你自身须行之事中。每一造物皆须做从其自身构造推演而出之事。

sections.english: Imagine you were now dead, or had not lived before this moment. Now view the rest of your life as a bonus, and live it as nature directs.
sections.chinese: 想象你此刻已死，或在此刻之前尚未活过。如今将你余生视为一笔额外之赏，并依自然所指引而度之。

sections.english: Love only what falls your way and is fated for you. What could suit you more than that?
sections.chinese: 只爱那些落入您途、且为您命定之物事。世间何物能比这更适宜于你？

sections.english: In every contingency keep in your mind's eye those who had the same experience before, and reacted with vexation, disbelief, or complaint. So where are they now? Nowhere. Well then, do you want to act like them? Why not leave the moods and shifts of others to those who are shifted by them, and concentrate on how to use these contingencies yourself?
sections.chinese: 每一变故中，留心回想那些曾有过同样经历、并以烦恼、不信或怨诉回应的人。那么他们如今在哪里？无处可觅。那你还要像他们那样行事吗？为何不把别人之情绪与摇摆留给那些被它们所摇摆之人，而专注于你自己如何运用此等变故？

sections.english: Dig inside yourself. Inside there is a spring of goodness ready to gush at any moment, if you keep digging.
sections.chinese: 向你自己内里开掘。你内里有一善之泉源，时时准备迸涌喷发，只要你持续挖掘。

sections.english: The body, too, should stay firmly composed, and not fling itself about either in motion or at rest. Just as the mind displays qualities in the face, keeping it intelligent and attractive, something similar should be required of the whole body. But all this should be kept in place without affectation.
sections.chinese: 身体也当保持稳固之镇宁，不于运动中或静止中甩掷动荡。正如心灵在面容上展露其品质，使之智慧而悦目，于整个躯体亦应有一类似之要求。然这一切都应保持着而无做作之态。

sections.english: The art of living is more like wrestling than dancing, in that it stands ready for what comes and is not thrown by the unforeseen.
sections.chinese: 生活之术，更似摔跤而非舞蹈，在于它随时备对即将到来之事，不为意外所颠扑。

sections.english: All the time you should consider who are these people whose endorsement you wish, and what are the minds that direct them. When you look into the sources of their judgement and impulse, you will not blame their unwitting error, nor will you feel the need of their endorsement.
sections.chinese: 时时刻刻，你当思忖：你所愿得其首肯之人，究是何等人，以及那引导他们之心灵究竟是什么。当你探看其判断与冲动之源头时，你便既不责其无意之过失，亦不觉需要其首肯。

sections.english: 'No soul', says Plato, 'likes to be robbed of truth' — and the same holds of justice, moderation, kindness, and all such virtues. Essential that you should keep this constantly in your mind: this will make you more gentle to all.
sections.chinese: 柏拉图说：「无一灵魂甘愿被剥夺真理」——此理于正义、节制、仁善，及所有此类美德，亦复如是。至关紧要的是你当时时铭记此念于心：这将使你对所有人皆更加温良。

sections.english: Whenever you suffer pain, have ready to hand the thought that pain is not a moral evil and does not harm your governing intelligence: pain can do no damage either to its rational or to its social nature. In most cases of pain you should be helped too by the saying of Epicurus: 'Pain is never unbearable or unending, as long as you remember its limits and do not add to it in your imagination.'
sections.chinese: 每当你遭遇痛楚，当备此念在手边：痛苦并非道德之恶，亦不损害你那统领之智识；痛苦绝难伤及它之理性或其社会本性。在多数痛苦之情形中，伊壁鸩鲁之语也当有助于你：「痛苦从非不堪忍受或永无竟时，只要你记住其界限，而不以你之想象增添于其上。」

sections.english: Take care that you never treat the misanthropic as they treat mankind.
sections.chinese: 注意己行，永勿以厌世者对待人类之方式来待人。

sections.english: How do we know that Telauges' character did not make him a better man than Socrates? It is not enough that Socrates died a more glorious death, that he argued more skilfully with the sophists, that he showed greater endurance in spending a whole night in the frost. The question is: what sort of soul did Socrates have? Could he be content with showing justice to men and piety to gods?
sections.chinese: 我们何以知道特拉乌格斯之品格并未令他成为比苏格拉底更好的人？苏格拉底死得更为荣耀，与智者们辩驳得更为精妙，能在霜冻中度过一整夜而展示出更大之坚忍——但仅此尚不足够。问题在于：苏格拉底拥有何等之灵魂？他是否能以施正义于人、虔敬于神而心满意足？

sections.english: The way nature has blended you into the compound whole does not prevent you drawing a boundary around yourself and keeping what is your own in your own control. Always remember this: remember too that the happy life depends on very little. And do not think that just because you have given up hope of being a scholar or a scientist, you should therefore despair of being free, sure of yourself, a social being, obedient to god.
sections.chinese: 自然将你混合入那复合整体之中的方式，并不妨碍你在己身周围划出界线，并将属于你自身之物守持在你自身之掌控下。当时时铭记此事：亦铭记幸福之生活仅依赖于极少之物。且勿以为，只因你放弃了成为学者或科学家之希望，你便也因此当对自由、自信、做一个社会性存在者、顺从于神而感到绝望。

sections.english: Live through your life without pressure and in the utmost contentment, even if all are clamouring what they will against you, even if wild beasts are tearing off the limbs of this poor lump of a body accreted round you. What in all this prevents the mind from keeping itself in a place of calm, with a true judgement on circumstance and ready use of all events submitted to it?
sections.chinese: 以无有压力、并极致满足之心，度过你之生命——即便众人在喧哗呐喊他们所意欲的、一切与你相悖之言，即便野兽正在撕扯这嵌在你周围之可怜肉块之四肢。在此一切之中，有什么能阻止那心灵将自身保持在平静之所，以对处境之真实判断和对一切提交于它之事变的善加利用？

sections.english: Perfection of character is this: to live each day as if it were your last, without frenzy, without apathy, without pretence.
sections.chinese: 品格之完美即在于此：将每一日当作最后一日光景般去过——无有狂躁，无有麻木，无有虚伪自欺。

sections.english: The gods, who are free from death, do not resent their need throughout all the length of eternity to tolerate in such numbers such worthless creatures as men: what is more, they even care for them in all sorts of ways. And do you, with the merest time before your own departure, refuse to bear with these worthless creatures — and one of them is you?
sections.chinese: 诸神，脱离了死亡之存在，亦不因在永恒之全部长度中须容耐如此众多、如此微不足道之造物如人类者而懊恼：更有甚者，他们还以诸般方式顾念他们。而你，在你自身离去之前仅剩这弹指之时光，却拒绝忍受这些微不足道之造物——况且，你自己亦是其中之一？

sections.english: It is ridiculous not to escape from one's own vices, which is possible, while trying to escape the vices of others, which is impossible.
sections.chinese: 不逃避自己之恶习——这是可能的——而竭力逃避他人之恶习——这却是不可能的：这是荒唐可笑之事。

sections.english: Whatever the rational and social faculty finds neither intelligent nor to the common good it judges, with good reason, beneath itself.
sections.chinese: 凡理性兼社会性之官能所发现为既非智性、亦不关乎公共福祉之物，它便以理据此判其为在其自身之下。

sections.english: When you have done good and another has benefited, why do you still look, as fools do, for a third thing besides — credit for good works, or a return?
sections.chinese: 当你行事为善、他人因之获益之后，为何你仍像愚人一般，再寻找第三样东西——为善行之赞誉，或回报？

sections.english: No one tires of receiving benefit: and action in accordance with nature is your own benefit. Do not then tire of benefit gained by benefit given.
sections.chinese: 无人会对受取好处感到厌倦：而依照自然之行动则是你自身之益处。那便不要厌倦于通过施与好处而获得之益处。

sections.english: The nature of the Whole set itself to create a universe. So now either everything that comes into being springs from that as logical consequence, or else even the primary aims to which the directing mind of the universe sets its own impulse are irrational. Remembrance of this will bring you to a calmer mind in many things.
sections.chinese: 宇宙整体之本性曾致力于创造一个宇宙。故如今，要么一切生成之物皆从彼作为逻辑之推论而生，要么即便是宇宙主导之心智为其自身冲动所设定的那些首要目的也是非理性的。记住这一点，将使你在许多事情上获得更平静之心智。
